title: KPI lifecycle decision fabric & launch gating sheet
content:
Purpose:
A compact lifecycle-to-KPI mapping and gating sheet designed to be a one-page decision fabric for launches. Maps phases -> signal thresholds -> immediate actions -> escalation path. Goal is to remove ambiguity during rapid traffic shifts and make rollback decisions measurable.

How to use (quick):
- Fill rows for each feature/route being launched.
- Populate baseline metrics from staging load tests.
- Agree warning/critical thresholds with SRE and product owner before canary.
- During rollout, monitor the signals column and follow the row's actions.

CSV table (copy into spreadsheet):
phase,route/feature,kpi,baseline,warning_threshold,critical_threshold,warning_action,critical_action,owner,racI_contact,pagerduty,notes
preflight,/api/generate,p99_latency_ms,120,250,500,stop_canary_and-investigate,rollback-to-previous-commit,Product Owner,Avery Chen,pd:infra,baseline from load-test-3
canary,/chat-stream,5xx_rate_pct,0.3,1.0,3.0,reduce_canary_traffic_by_50%,cut_traffic_to_zero_and-failover-to-hosted,Eng-SRE,Jonas Meyer,pd:sre,collect kv-cache metrics + recent model diff
ramp,/embed-bulk,median_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,0.65,0.95,1.40,apply-caching-profile,scale-dedicated-pool or enable-quantized-variant,Product Ops,Priya Kapoor,pd:ops,evaluate per-customer cost alerts
scale,/search-rerank,model_eval_pass_rate_pct,98,95,90,notify-model-team-and-enable-strict-filtering,rollback-model-and-blacklist-last-deploy,Applied ML,Maya Rodriguez,pd:ml,compare eval-set drift + human-review
steady_state,/public-api,error_budget_pct_used,12,30,60,trigger-rate-limiting,activate-sla-escalation-and-customer-communication,Customer Success,Alex Kim,pd:cs,apply long-tail mitigation plan

Decision rules (engineered):
- Warning actions are immediate mitigations that preserve user experience (traffic shaping, throttles, reduced concurrency).
- Critical actions are fail-closed behaviors (full rollback, route disable, model fallback).
- All thresholds should be expressed as percentiles or absolute values with a simple measurement window (e.g., p99 over last 5m, rolling 15m average).
- If multiple KPIs cross critical thresholds simultaneously, assume highest-severity action (e.g., rollback) unless explicit owner trumps.

Preflight checklist (to run 24–72h before canary):
- [ ] Smoke test (single request) against canary variant (succeeds 100% for baseline prompts)
- [ ] Load profile run (75th, 90th, 99th percentile sequences) completed and results attached
- [ ] Cost projection vs. baseline for first 100k requests generated
- [ ] Observability hooks validated (tracing, token-level cost, model-diff beacon)
- [ ] Canary cohort identified and runtime feature flag configured
- [ ] Incident playbook reviewed and PoC assigned (see linked artifacts)

Runbook snippets (short):
- If p99 latency > warning_threshold: reduce canary traffic by 50% via rollout controller, open a high-priority bug in JIRA (PRODOPS-<n>), tag with `rollout-impact`.
- If p99 latency > critical_threshold: pause rollout, notify on-call SRE, trigger rollback job (automated pipeline). Communicate to stakeholder channel (#prodops-launches) with template: "Rollback initiated for <route> — reason: latency critical at <value>ms — action: reverting to <commit>".

Escalation matrix (contact order):
1) On-call SRE (pagerduty: pd:sre)
2) Product Owner (owner column)
3) Applied ML lead (if model quality regression)
4) CS Tier 2 (if customer-facing SLA impacted)
5) Exec on-call (if >30% user impact or revenue signal)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Define canonical measurement window for "cost per 1k tokens" (rolling 1h vs 24h) — recommend rolling 1h for fast feedback.
- Add automated notebook that pulls the last 3 canary runs and computes warning/critical percentiles (Jonas to prototype).
- Determine whether to auto-scale dedicated pool on cost or on latency first (trade-off doc needed).

Attachments & quick links:
- confluence:prodops/decision-fabric-v1 (design doc)
- jira:PRODOPS-1023 (related decision tickets)
- github:infra/rollout-playbooks#45 (automation for rollback)

Author notes: this sheet is intentionally compact. Keep a single canonical copy per launch and snapshot to confluence after stability is reached (tag: snapshot YYYYMMDD).
